newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Hansa declines new Estonia Savings Bank stock.
newsitem.headline: Hansa declines new Estonia Savings Bank stock.

text.p: Leading Estonian bank Hansapank and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) said on Tuesday they were unlikely to take part in an issue of new stock in another big bank, Savings Bank.

Savings Bank is to issue 3.2 million shares at 33.50 kroons each. Current shareholders can subscribe for new shares in proportion to their existing holdings. Hansapank and the EBRD both own 21.05 percent of Savings Bank.
"I cannot see any need to increase our equities investment portfolio and there is no need for strategic investment like earlier," Hansapank director general Juri Mois told Reuters.
He said the shares were also available on the stock exchange.
EBRD representative Andre Kuusvek also said the EBRD was unlikely to buy more shares although a final decision has not been made.
"The situation does not demand our intervention as the Savings Bank is stable enough and there is no need for an immediate increase in the share capital," he said.
Savings Bank is planning to merge with Estonia's eighth largest bank, the Bank of Industry, and also recently bought the former state-owned insurance company.
